title: Pedestrian Crossings
whatItIs: Zebra and parallel crossings have no lights for traffic; the others are signal-controlled.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT park on a crossing or in the zig-zag area, before or after it.
You MUST NOT overtake the moving vehicle nearest the crossing, or one stopped to give way.
A straight-across pelican is one crossing even with an island: you MUST wait for people coming from the far side.

keyFacts: A zebra with a central island, or a staggered signal crossing, is two separate crossings.
Give way to anyone still crossing after your signal changes to green, at any crossing.

visual.caption: What traffic sees at each crossing

rows: MUST give way once a pedestrian is on it
MUST give way to pedestrians and cyclists on it
Flashing amber: MUST give way to anyone on it
For horse riders: wider crossing space

b.label: Puffin
points: Signals above the button, on the near side

onTheTest.question: At a pelican crossing the amber light is flashing and a pedestrian is still crossing. What must you do?
options: Sound the horn to warn them
Move off as the amber starts
onTheTest.why: Rule 196: when the amber is flashing you MUST give way to any pedestrians on the crossing. Go on with caution only if it's clear.

onTheTest.question: Your pupil waves a pedestrian across a zebra crossing. How should you explain why this is wrong?
options: Another vehicle may come and not stop
Only police may wave people over
Pedestrians must wait for a gap
Waving is only allowed at night
onTheTest.why: Rule 195: don't wave, flash your lights or sound your horn to invite people across: it could be dangerous if another vehicle is approaching.

traps: Zebra: traffic must stop once someone is on it, but you should give way to people waiting.
Toucan, puffin and equestrian crossings have no flashing amber phase.
Don't rev your engine or edge forward to hurry pedestrians.
